title: Never mutate workflow state from a read path (+ a latent migration defect it had masked)
commit_subject: 0.7.1: never mutate workflow state from a read path
trigger: External review I7 verdict: current behaviour not acceptable; handle before S1-A, at minimum before the real A/B/R originals are opened by v10 code.

changes.factory_core/storage.py: _upgrade_schema is DDL-only (no rebase, no event, no revision); v8->v9 back-fill guarded by `if current < 9:`; status_snapshot enforces monotonic effect-domain generation
changes.diffstat_caveat: Most of storage.py's 733-line diff is the 4-space re-indent of the 336-line v8->v9 back-fill block; the logic change there is the single guard.

i7_direct_fix.problem: _upgrade_schema() is reached by 40 call sites, many of them pure read entry points (load, status_snapshot, events, dirty_flags, stage_checkpoints, ...). It ran the classifier rebase, appending DIRTY_CLASSIFIER_REBASED and incrementing the business revision.
i7_direct_fix.rejected_alternative: deferring the rebase into the next business write transaction is NOT viable: transition() enforces row['revision'] == expected_revision, so a revision-bumping rebase inside that transaction makes every queued transition raise RevisionConflict.
i7_direct_fix.adopted: migration = DDL only; rebase is an explicit maintenance action (SQLiteStateStore.rebase_dirty_classifier + new `factory rebase-classifier` CLI entry). The method previously had no production caller and no CLI entry, so the capability was unreachable.

latent_defect_exposed.symptom: After removing the automatic rebase, A/B/R copies diverged: B and R reported aggregate_valid=false while A stayed true.
latent_defect_exposed.root_cause: _upgrade_schema contained a 336-line v8->v9 data back-fill with NO source-version guard, so any later migration re-ran it. It INSERTs into tables that are themselves effect-hash domains (stage_checkpoint_history, dirty_causes, workflow_decision_requests/_instances, solver_jobs) and UPDATEs project_state/solver_jobs. B and R were created directly on v9, so they had never run the back-fill; their first 9->10 migration appended 13 checkpoint history rows, changing the checkpoint_history domain with no event re-attesting the hash.
latent_defect_exposed.why_previously_hidden: the migration's trailing rebase event computes effect_hashes_after AFTER all mutations, so it silently re-attested the changed domains. That event had been masking a pre-existing defect; removing it merely made the defect visible.
latent_defect_exposed.fix: guard the whole back-fill block with `if current < 9:` -- storage.py, 336 lines re-indented.

verification_on_real_history_copies.method: copy each project's .factory/state.db to /tmp, open with v10 code, inspect the copy. Originals untouched.
verification_on_real_history_copies.conclusion: A 9->10 migration is now DDL-only: no workflow state change, no event, no revision move, and the historical aggregate check stays valid.

other_items.I2_domain_monotonicity: status_snapshot() now asserts the effect-domain key set never shrinks across the event stream. Test test_effect_domain_generation_must_be_monotonic builds the case where the tolerance branch itself would pass, proving the invariant is what rejects it.
other_items.I5_write_entry_3: final_evidence_recovery now records classification_source='bespoke_recovery'; write-entry 2 (v8->v9 historical reconstruction) deliberately still records nothing, so legacy_unrecorded now means exactly 'created before the provenance contract, or reconstructed by a historical migration'.
other_items.I6_db_level_rollback: test_provenance_insert_rejected_at_db_level_rolls_back_cause installs a BEFORE INSERT ... RAISE(ABORT) trigger on the provenance table and asserts neither the cause nor its provenance lands.
other_items.Concurrency: not re-tested here; the existing test_concurrent_transitions_* series covers revision CAS.

available_exit_conditions.failed_migration_rolls_back: PASS (test_failed_migration_rolls_back_completely, injection point moved to ensure_dirty_cause_classification_schema because the rebase no longer runs)

test_baseline.note: 0.7.1 touched the migration (40 call sites), status_snapshot, the recovery path and the CLI, with zero regressions.

open_items: True binary/code-version downgrade regression still pending: run bde49712's code as a separate interpreter against a schema-10 fixture and assert it refuses before any business write.
Reviewer question I9: does aggregate_valid need to distinguish 'chain self-consistent' from 'self-consistent as of the last write'? Before this fix, the trailing rebase re-attested mutated domains.
Reviewer question I8: are there other unguarded migration-time data writes besides the guarded block?
